name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design

platform.note: PSI search record gives the flight platform as the ISS; the PSI record also lists drop-tower tests on the ground.

objective.value: Obtain soot-inception limits, detailed measurements and extinction limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames (ethylene, methane; also coflow flames) as functions of flow rate, stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst), inert amount (N2 or CO2) and pressure; identify hot-region temperatures and whether extinction is radiative or kinetic, and test for pseudo-flammability limits.

safety_functions.note: Deduction, not stated by a source: PSI-10 is a fundamental gaseous-flame study (soot inception, radiative/kinetic extinction, steady spherical flames) and no source assigns it a prevention, detection or suppression role. airflow.note: No airflow velocity is reported anywhere I read. The PSI experimental tables give reactant mass flow rates (mfuel/mN2/mtot in mg/s), not a chamber airflow, and these are burner-fed spherical flames in a quiescent CIR chamber; so the field is left unknown rather than recording a mass flow as airflow (units would not match the habitat scenarios).

notes: o2_percent and pressure_psi are left as seed (unknown) on purpose: scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py overwrites them from data/source/psi/tables/conditions.json, which has a PSI-10 entry. Not hand-edited (AGENTS.md rule 11).

Fuel conflict: the PSI objective names ethylene (C2H4) and methane (CH4); the per-test experimental tables list ethylene (C2H4) and propane (C3H8). Both are recorded at confidence medium rather than picking one silently.
airflow is unknown: the PSI tables report reactant mass flow rates in mg/s, not a chamber airflow velocity, so no airflow value was recorded.
gravity_g = 0 g is taken from PSI Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation' plus the drop-tower/ISS approach; no partial-gravity claim is made.

All PSI facts come from the local files (data/source/psi/PSI-10.json, PSI-10.search.json, tables/PSI-10.csv and PSI-10_2.csv). No psi.nasa.gov page was loaded. The one web fetch was the NASA ACME project overview PDF, which describes ACME generally, not Flame Design tests specifically.
Data files not downloaded: the record lists 3,807 files totalling about 2.18 TB; only names, counts, formats and sizes were recorded.
share of sourced fields: 15/18 (o2_percent, pressure_psi and airflow are unknown).
